questions.question: Which of these helps direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning on highways?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows on the road show which lanes are for going straight or turning.

questions.question: When can you text while driving?

options.text: Any time if you are under 18.
Any time if you are 18 or older.
If you can text without looking at your phone.

questions.explanation: You cannot text while driving except in emergencies. Taking your eyes off the road increases the chance of a crash.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive no faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back into your eyes and make it harder to see.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving?
questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect driving. This includes illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is illegal.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Signal to tell them when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and slow down to let them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane and slow down when another driver passes you. This makes it easy for them to return to your lane safely.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.

questions.explanation: Two solid yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. Never cross these lines to pass other vehicles.

questions.question: It starts raining while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: Slow down when it rains. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is very heavy, pull to the shoulder and stop until it clears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a right turn at this intersection.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers keeping a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for the road conditions. Always follow speed limits and drive slower when conditions are poor.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and go when the way is clear.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "be careful." Slow down, look around, and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What can help drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.

questions.explanation: Quick stops waste fuel because you must accelerate again to match traffic speed. Drivers who look ahead can slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid hard braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a curve or hill because another vehicle is unlikely to be coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
When your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane ahead is clear.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never drive on the shoulder to pass. You cannot pass when there is a solid yellow line.

questions.question: Why should you be alert to motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
Motorcycle riders are less skilled than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and easier to miss than cars. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away they are or how fast they are going. Always watch for motorcycles.

questions.question: When you are in traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your vehicle can cross all the way without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross all the way without stopping.
questions.explanation: Check that you have enough space to cross completely before entering the tracks. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they must do. It means left turns are not allowed here.

questions.question: If you stop on the side of the road at night:

options.text: Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beam headlights on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and keep low beam headlights on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and low beam headlights so other drivers can see you clearly at night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Signal when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your horn when needed. This helps other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you are doing.

questions.question: You reach an intersection with a flashing red light. You must:

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Then proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic. You must also always yield to pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving ability compared to other things?

options.text: The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.explanation: Fatigue affects your driving the same way alcohol does. Being awake for 18 hours impairs your driving as much as having a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours straight has the same effect as a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: What should you do if a car is heading straight toward you in your lane?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.

questions.explanation: First, honk your horn to get the other driver's attention. If they don't move, steer to the right. Steering left is dangerous because if the other driver moves last second, you will still crash. If a crash seems unavoidable, brake hard and steady. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: You find a problem with your vehicle that could affect safety. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have money.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any problem that could affect safe driving must be fixed as soon as possible. Fix the problem before you drive the vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest season to drive in.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
It is safe to use cruise control in winter weather.
Snow tires are the best choice for winter.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use cruise control in winter weather.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter is the hardest driving season and needs extra care. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often. Snow tires help your vehicle grip slippery roads better.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a marked crosswalk.
